title: Windows: tests that read golden/fixture text fail under Git's default core.autocrlf=true (.gitattributes misses post goldens, .mch and .step fixtures)

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:low
labels.description: Mechanical, one file, no new logic (issue-worker-low)

body:
Found by the new Windows check (Windows 11, Git for Windows defaults: `core.autocrlf=true`), main 380c29b3c, `cargo xtask gate quick`.

## What happens

Git for Windows checks text files out with CRLF by default. `.gitattributes` pins `crates/app/tests/golden/**`, tester kits, examples and `*.sh` to LF, but not every fixture that tests compare byte for byte or parse. Four suites (17 tests) fail on such a checkout, each within a second:

| Suite | Reads | Pinned? |
|---|---|---|
| post `explain_fanuc_family`, `explain_remaining` | `crates/post/tests/golden/explain/*.nc` | **no** |
| app `wire_taper_angle` | `crates/app/tests/edm/wire-iso-fixture.mch` (include_str) | **no** |
| app `import_step_curve_guard` | `testdata/models/box.step` (include_str) | **no** |

Example: `fanuc_explain_golden_preserves_program` - left (generated) ends lines with `\n`, right (golden from the checkout) with `\r\n`; the content is otherwise identical.

## Fix

Pin every byte-compared or parsed text fixture to LF, e.g.:

```
crates/*/tests/golden/** text eol=lf
crates/*/tests/**/*.mch  text eol=lf
testdata/**/*.step       text eol=lf
testdata/**/*.stp        text eol=lf
```

(or one broader rule for `crates/*/tests/**` and `testdata/**`), then `git add --renormalize .`. A unit test in xtask (or a CI-free check) could assert that `git check-attr eol` is `lf` for every file under the golden/fixture dirs.

## Done means

On a fresh Windows checkout with `core.autocrlf=true`, the four suites above pass; `git check-attr eol -- <each fixture>` reports `lf`.

title: Bore: a helical strategy (continuous helix to full depth, then a floor circle)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
### What are you trying to do

Counterbores for M6 cap screws in aluminium: Ø11 × 7 deep, cut with a Ø6 flat end mill on a small 3-axis mill (LinuxCNC, ER20 spindle). The usual way to cut these is helical interpolation: the tool spirals down on the wall radius to full depth, then runs one flat circle at the floor. It never plunges straight into solid material.

In 0.24.0 the Bore operation is a level-by-level ring ladder. At each step-down level the tool dives at the hole centre, sweeps out to the wall and runs a ring, then moves to the next level. The source describes the first engagement as the bore's centre dive, and the Lead-in tab has no entry choice for Bore. Linking → Level to level → Helix helps between levels, but that helix runs on a 1 mm radius at the centre and the first dive is still a plunge. With a 1 mm step-down that comes to 7 plunges and 7 rings per counterbore.

On a light machine, a flat end mill plunging into solid aluminium is the move most likely to chatter, pack chips or snap the tool. That's why the helical cycle is the default for counterbores and holes bored with an end mill.

### How you imagine it working

A **Helical** strategy in the Bore operation (or a separate Helical bore operation):

- The tool positions over the hole at the retract plane and descends on a **continuous helix** whose radius puts the cutter's rim on the finished wall (hole radius − tool radius − stock to leave), from Top Z to the hole floor.
- **Helix pitch** (mm per turn) is set by the user, with a sensible automatic value. Alternatively a maximum ramp angle.
- At the floor, **one full flat circle** to remove the ramp step, then a move off the wall towards the centre before retracting.
- Optional **spring pass**: a second floor circle with no extra depth.
- **Climb or conventional**, as Bore has now.
- For holes too wide for one helix to clear the core (wider than about 2 × tool diameter): helix at an inner radius first, then step out in rings at the floor, or simply refuse with a clear message.
- **Through holes:** continue the helix past the floor by the break-through allowance.

The rest of Bore can stay as it is (hole detection, per-hole floors, the reach checks).

Happy to test builds on the counterbore case above and air-cut the result on my machine.

body:
Implement the core 4-axis cylindrical flow-line toolpath kernel in `crates/motion/src/multiaxis/rotary_flow.rs`.

What to build:
- Accept picked 3D guide edge chains, part facets, a rotary `Axis` (provided by the #2772 stated-axis resolver), `RotaryFlowParams`, and `AxisControl`.
- Require a ball-nose tool and at least two guide chains in this first slice; refuse empty, off-model, or single-chain inputs by name.
- Unwrap each chain into continuous cylindrical `(theta, v)` coordinates about `Axis` using `unwrap_near`, and align chain pairs by nearest `2 * pi` offset.
- Parameterize the pair by normalized arc length, compute developed width `(s = R_ref * theta, v)`, and choose pass count from `stepover` or `scallop_stepover(r, tolerance)`.
- Adaptively chord each interpolated flow curve within `ARC_FIT_TOL` / `tolerance`.
- Compute gouge-free radial ball centers `rho_ball(theta, v)` where `min_tri dist(center, tri) >= r` via `closest_pt_tri`, so steep helical flanks never gouge.
- Link passes radially on the retract cylinder (matching `rotary_links`) and emit tool tips via `retip` and `command_axis`.

Provenance: published 4-axis cylindrical unwrapping and iso-parametric flow-line CAM literature; no vendor material consulted.

Depends on #2772 for stated rotary axis resolution on helical models.

body:
Follow-up of #2727 (PR #2788).

## What happens

`xtask/src/budget.rs` sets the gate's job budget to a fixed `DEFAULT` of 6 when `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS` is not set. The batch and release tiers split that budget over at most 3 lanes. On a big machine most cores then stay idle.

Measured on the post-merge runner wopr (Ryzen 9 5950X, 16 cores / 32 threads, 125 GB), head `1da2bcca2` of #2788, warm cache, all green, 929 steps:

| Budget | Batch wall time |
|---|---|
| serial (before #2788) | 73 min |
| default 6 | 30.8 min (load ~15 of 32) |
| `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=32` | **14.4 min** |

Today every runner needs `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS` in its `.env` (wopr 32, uma 16, m3 16, len 8 are set by hand), and a contributor's machine never gets more than 6.

## Wanted

- When `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS` is not set, the default budget is the number of available CPUs (`std::thread::available_parallelism()`), with a floor of 2 and an upper cap (for example 64).
- Optionally a memory guard: no more parallel test lanes than the free memory allows (each heavy suite needs ~2-4 GB), so a 32-thread box with 16 GB does not swap.
- The lane count follows the budget (today at most 3 lanes); the `ISOLATED` steps, builds, ui steps and clippy still run alone with the whole budget.
- `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS` still overrides; the plan (`--dry-run`) prints the chosen budget and where it came from.
- AGENTS.md / the `gate` skill say the default is now the core count (process change: PROCESS_VERSION bump at merge).

## Done means

On a machine without the variable, `cargo xtask gate batch --dry-run` shows a budget equal to the core count (within the cap and memory guard); a unit test pins the default (mock CPU and memory values), the override and the floor/cap; the existing lane tests stay green.

title: 3D Finish: an option to stop the waterline ring pass on steep flanks

labels.name: claimed
labels.description: An agent is working on this - see the claim comment

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
## What is asked

A contributor asks for one control on 3D Finish: a switch that turns off the waterline ring pass, so the operation cuts its raster lines only. The contributor's words, quoted unchanged (chat, 2026-11-19):

> how hard would it be to make a checkbox that can disable the waterline portion?

## What the tool does today

A Parallel 3D Finish operation splits the terrain at 45 degrees. Shallow facets get the Z-following raster lines. Steep facets get waterline rings: `parallel()` runs one raster pass, then `rings_and_tail` (`crates/motion/src/finishing3d/raster.rs` line 210). The ring paths run about 90 degrees across the raster lines. Every wall that stands above the Bottom plane gets its ring ladder: hole walls, end walls, and the sloped edges of a tilted top face.

The picture below shows a contributor's test part: a long bar with a top face tilted 2 degrees and two openings, cut with a 0.3125 in ball-end, Bottom 0.300 in. The purple arrow marks one ring run that still survives on a wall near the near end. The tall ladders at the far end wall are the same law at the high end of the sloped face. The raster family cannot cover those walls; only the rings can.

![Ring run surviving on a wall at Bottom 0.300 in, parallel to the bar length and near the near end edge](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FlamingFireCoding/Camcraft/screenshots/issue-2811-waterline-arrow.png)

## Why the switch is wanted

On a part whose steep flanks are out of scope, the rings add cutting time, and they add paths the machinist did not ask for. Some machinists want the lines only, and accept the walls as they stand. One checkbox should say that choice out loud.

## Proposed shape

- One parameter, for example `waterlines: bool`, default on. Existing behaviour does not change.
- GUI name: not just "off". The control must name the consequence, for example "Steep flanks: Waterlines / Leave uncut".
- The switch applies to the Parallel pattern. Whether Parallel multi and Scallop take it is a decision. Blend should likely never take it: its 30-45 degree double cut needs the rings to remove the staircase (its own note says so). The maintainer decides this scope.

## Laws the switch must keep

1. With the switch off and steep flanks present, the path must carry a visible note that names the uncut flanks and their count. Silent rest material is not allowed (Prime Directive).
2. A model that is fully steep with the switch off must refuse with a clear error, not post an empty program. The raster answers `false` for an all-steep model; today "the rings alone carry it".
3. The parameter round-trips in the project file. Old project files load with the default, on.
4. The 3D finish MCP parameter surface exposes the same field (same rule as `fill_openings` and `gap_link`).

## Measured support (headless probe, main `744c0847b`)

Synthetic model: bar 24 x 160 mm, flat bottom z 0, top face sloped 2 degrees, two through openings, ball 7.94 mm, Parallel, gap link Jump. The probe classifies the XY direction of every Feed move.

- Bottom 0: 188 along-wall Y-family Feed runs at Z ladder levels about 0.4 mm apart. Zero Feed runs cross the open top face. All perpendicular feed sits on walls.
- Bottom raised to 9.75 mm (near the high top edge): the same perpendicular runs collapse to three ladder levels per wall, and only over the stretch where the face still stands above Bottom. Nothing sits in the open middle.

This matches the picture: raising Bottom shrank the ring set everywhere except where walls still rise above it. The behaviour is correct as designed; this issue asks for control, not for a defect fix. The probe code can become the pinning test for the switch.

## Done means

- A checkbox flips the ring pass on and off, and each state has a motion test that pins it.
- Off plus steep flanks: a note names the uncut flanks; no ring moves appear in the CL output.
- Off plus a steep-only model: a refusal with a clear message.
- Project-file round-trip test and MCP parity pass.
- The 3D finish page shows the control with its consequence wording.

## Classification

This account is a contributor and cannot set labels. Suggested labels, for a maintainer: `enhancement`, `P6`, `effort:high` (safety floor: it changes posted G-code when the switch is used), `area:motion`, `area:ui`, `area:mcp`. The body was written by the contributor's agent at the contributor's request.

body:
**What happens:** `cargo xtask gate batch` (and every gate built on it: merge trains, post-merge checks) runs its ~620 steps strictly one after another (`xtask/src/exec.rs`, "the one-at-a-time loop"). Each step compiles and links one test binary, then runs it. Linking a large Rust test binary uses about one core.

**Evidence (2026-11-19, merge train on a 16-core Hetzner ccx43, main 409c0b5ab + one PR):**
- 1 h 20 min wall time; load average 2.7-2.8 on 16 cores for most of the run; the provider's CPU graph sits at ~100-300 % of 1600 %.
- At the moment checked: step 623 (`app suites: pocket3d_reach`), one `rustc` at 100 %, nothing else busy.
- `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=16` was set; it scales `-j` and `--test-threads` inside a step, but the steps themselves do not overlap.

The release tier already has parallel lanes (#2057, the longest-first queue of #2461), which took the release gate from 114.6 to 52.7 min. The batch tier does not use them.

**Proposal (two parts, either helps):**
1. **One parallel prebuild:** before the steps, build every test binary the plan needs in one cargo call (`cargo test --no-run -j N` over the planned packages/targets, with the same profile and features the steps use, so the steps reuse the artifacts instead of relinking one by one).
2. **Lanes for batch:** run the batch steps through the release queue's lanes (longest first, sharing the job budget), so several test binaries run at once.

Keep what the gate guarantees today: every step still runs and is logged, a red step still fails the gate, VOID detection is unchanged.

**Done means:** `cargo xtask gate batch` on a 16-core host uses most of its cores during the build phase, and its wall time drops substantially against the same commit (measure before/after on the same machine; numbers in the PR).

Related: #2461, #2057, #2556, #2557.

body:
Sew XYUV rulings consistently across planes when one plane heals a swallowtail and the other plane does not.

## Context

When XY trims a tight corner fillet or bridges a shallow slot, its offset ring `wu`/`wl` loses arc length while UV keeps the full arc. Pairing directly by trimmed offset arc length (`crates/motion/src/wire_edm/pairing.rs`) shifts rulings out of phase around the contour and can trigger `folds`, `crossing`, or `too_far`. Also, `ruled_widen::away` (`crates/motion/src/wire_edm/ruled_widen.rs`) computes widening directions from unhealed `given` edges, which can reverse steps near a trimmed vertex.

## What this does

- Build a monotone preimage map from each healed offset ring's edge midpoints and vertices back to arc positions on its original input profile `given`.
- Collapse any excised input span `(s_a, s_b)` to the corresponding trimmed intersection vertex `V_trim` so `ArcLength` and `SyncPoints` pairings generate clean cone/fan rulings from `V_trim` to the opposing plane (`pairing.rs` and `ruled.rs`).
- Snap sync points that fall inside an excised corner span directly to `V_trim` instead of shifting across adjacent flanks.
- Update `ruled_widen::away` to derive the outward miter/offset direction from the surviving offset ring segments at trimmed vertices so per-ruling widening does not reverse or tangle.
- Verify all ruled-surface laws (`folds`, `crossing`, `lean_law`, and 33-height `clearance` against the unhealed `product` surface) on the sewn rulings.

## Done means:

- Asymmetric XY/UV shapes (for example a sharp inside corner or tight fillet on XY paired with an open fillet on UV) generate clean fan rulings without phase drift, false folds, or widening reversals.
- `clearance` catches mid-height wall gouges from bridging across a deep slot on one plane and refuses them by name.

The public Sodick "Wire EDM Machine Operation Training, LN1W / LN2W Control" manual (part number 6300015, 2012) shows a program example that changes the flushing for the finish passes. The project has no parameter for the flushing of a skim pass.

## Done means

- A skim pass can state its flushing (from the machine file condition or an operation parameter, by a decision).
- The Sodick post writes that T word before the skim's C word, or refuses by name when the value is not known.
- A pinning test and a golden in `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/sodick-wire/`.

## Notes

- This changes posted G-code, so the safety floor applies (`effort:high`).
- Until then, the program header tells the operator to set the flushing at the control when no word is stated.
- Refs #2649.

title: Engrave typed text on a face: type a string, pick the face and spot, set height and tool

labels.name: in-review
labels.description: Fix pushed on a branch with an open PR; merges at the next cut

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
Filed by the maintainer in chat (2026-11-19): "I want to be able to type text, select a face and location for the text, text size and a tool and it does the engraving. It's common for people to want engraved part numbers but it isn't modeled."

## What the user wants

1. Type a text string, for example a part number `SN-0471`.
2. Pick the face to engrave and place the text on that face.
3. Set the text height and the tool.
4. CamCraft makes the engraving toolpath, verifies it and posts it.

## What exists today

- `OpType::Engrave` and `OpType::Trace` machine 2D geometry along the tool centreline. They obey the mark law (#1595): a shallow mark passes, a deep cut is refused.
- 2D geometry comes from a DXF sketch (the `Sketch` entity, #1862). Work to feed sketch chains to Engrave and Trace is #1869. SVG import is #1880.
- There is no way to make geometry by typing text. A user today must draw the letters in a CAD program, export a DXF, and import it.

## What to build

- A text-to-outline step: convert the typed string into glyph outlines as 2D regions (outer loop + hole loops for letters such as A, B, O). Use one of the fonts already bundled in `assets/ui/fonts/`; the outlines are the same vectors the UI draws. Flatten the glyph curves to polylines within the setup tolerance. Clean-room: only the font's own licensed outlines, no vendor letter shapes.
- An undoable command (for example `InsertText`): the text string, height, and the placement become a `Sketch` the operation kinds already read. Ship its MCP tool with it (#128 law).
- Placement: select a planar face (or the setup top plane) in the viewport, then set X/Y and rotation. The existing `sketch::face_frame` code gives the face frame.
- Parameters on the Engrave operation: text string, height (mm or inch through the unit lens), letter spacing, depth (bounded by the mark law), tool, feed, and climb. The toolpath path is the existing Engrave/Trace generator.
- Two ride modes later, both from the same outlines: ride the glyph boundary with a small end mill or v-bit, and single-line engraving on the glyph skeleton with a v-bit. Pick one for the first cut; record the choice in `docs/decisions/`.

## Suggested label triage

`enhancement`, `area:2d`, `P6`, `effort:high` (safety floor: new toolpath and posted G-code). The filing account has no label rights; a collaborator sets these.

## Done means

The user types a string, picks a face and a spot, sets a height and a tool, and CamCraft generates, verifies and posts an engraving toolpath. A golden test pins the CL output for a known string and font. The placement, `.camproj` round-trip and MCP tests pass.

> issue, p4, we should add the ability to "rotate" part to the movement gizmo we added.

## State of the code (check first)

- #2047 (closed) added rotate handles for a part, as slice c of #1198. PR #2185 merged the ring handles and a Rotate button in the floating bar. #2514 lists owed items for them.
- #1198 (open) is the umbrella: "drag a body with gizmo handles (move and rotate), with a floating control bar".
- The maintainer asks for rotate on the movement gizmo itself. So the user must be able to rotate a part without a mode switch or a separate Rotate button.

The first agent that works this issue reads the current viewport code and the build that the maintainer uses. It writes in an issue comment what already exists and what the maintainer cannot reach. If the rotate handles already sit on the move gizmo, the agent says so, names the gap that remains (for example visibility, discoverability or the axis choice), and fixes that gap.

## Wanted

1. The movement gizmo for a selected part shows rotate handles at the same time as the move arrows: one ring for each axis (X, Y, Z of the part frame, or of the setup WCS, as the move gizmo uses).
2. A drag on a ring turns the part about the part centre, about that axis. The preview is live. The turn is shown in degrees. Typing a value is possible, as with the move distance.
3. A modifier snaps the turn to a step (for example 15 degrees). The step is a parameter with a default.
4. Move and rotate go through the undoable commands, one undo step for each drag. The existing move command and its MCP tool stay. A turn about the part centre uses the same command and tool as the existing rotate (`move_model` with a pivot). Add an MCP verb only if the agent surface lacks one (see the optional item in #2514).
5. A ring seen end-on (within a few degrees of the view direction) does not offer a drag that cannot turn. Show a hint. This is an owed item of #2514: do it here or reference it.
6. Plain English labels and tooltips. AccessKit nodes for each handle. No G-code words in UI text.

- A rotated part changes the toolpath inputs. The operations of that part must be marked stale or recomputed by the existing rules. Never keep a toolpath that was made for the old pose without a mark.
- Keep each source file under about 400 lines. `viewport_bar.rs` is already over (see #2514): split it along its seam.

- Layers: ui calls app commands. No direct write to the part transform from the UI.

## Done means

- A test shows that dragging a ring turns the part about the chosen axis by the dragged angle, and that undo restores the pose.
- A test shows the snap step and the typed value.
- A test shows that the operations of the part are marked stale after the turn.
- The PR body has the before and after screenshots.

title: 3D finishing: GPU inverse-offset height bound as a first filter for the f64 drop-cutter

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

labels.name: P4
labels.description: Work the maintainer asked for, for the next cut

body:
Part of #2526 (GPU shader toolpath generation). Slice 3 of 5. Needs #2619 (CPU facet grid) and #2620 (compute seam).

Maintainer order (2026-11-18): "GPU shader issues get priority". Thus this issue is `P4`.

## What
- A compute kernel computes, for each cell of a tile, a conservative bound of the ball support height: the inverse tool offset of the facets on a grid (M. Inui, "Fast inverse offset computation using polygon rendering hardware", Computer-Aided Design 35(2), 2003; the Z-map model of B. K. Choi and R. B. Jerard, "Sculptured Surface Machining", 1998).
- f32, tile-relative coordinates. The margin is larger than the stated f32 error bound of the kernel (WGSL "Floating Point Accuracy": division 2.5 ULP, `inverseSqrt` 2 ULP). The PR states the bound and how the margin covers it.
- The CPU uses the bound only to skip facets in `support_at` (`crates/motion/src/finishing3d/support.rs` 368-388) that cannot be the highest support.
- The posted height stays the f64 `support_at` value at the true sample point. `ball_clear` (lines 132-142) stays the certifier, in f64, against every facet of the CPU grid near the ball. The GPU never removes a facet from `ball_clear`.
- The app makes the GPU result in the generate job (`crates/app/src/commands/operation/generate.rs`), once for each operation, and passes it to motion as a value. Never in a frame. The CLI and MCP use the same path.
- With no GPU, or with the GPU off, motion runs the #2619 CPU path. The result is the same bytes.

## Prime Directive
- A wrong bound can only skip the true support. Then `ball_clear` refuses the lower candidate, and the march searches higher or refuses by name. A GPU error cannot make a gouge pass. A test pins this with a deliberately wrong bound (a fault injection test).
- The tolerance is not tied to the grid resolution. The grid only filters.

## Pinning tests (CPU reference)
- GPU on and GPU off give the same `.cl` and `.cnc` bytes on the 3D finishing goldens of `crates/app/tests/golden/`. Run on the software adapter; on hardware where present.
- The fault injection test above: a bound raised by a large value gives a refusal or the same output, never a lower cutter.
- Skip and fail policy of `headless_gpu` (#615, `CAMCRAFT_REQUIRE_GPU=1`).

## Readings
Time of one large 3D finishing operation: CPU grid only (#2619) against CPU grid plus GPU filter, release build, with upload and readback times. If the GPU does not gain on the large fixtures, the PR says so and the switch stays off by default.

## Decision entry
Only if a new crate edge is added past the ones of #2620.

Effort: `effort:max` (toolpath geometry algorithm on a new compute path; safety floor).

Done means: the GPU bound filters the support scan, the goldens are byte-equal with the GPU on and off, the fault injection test passes, and the PR states the readings.

title: Machine file: reserved tool numbers (the probe's pocket), so a cutting tool is never given that T number

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
## What happens

`add_tool` gives each new tool the lowest unused number from 1 (camcraft-mcp skill: "Assigns the lowest unused tool number in 1-99999"). Many machines keep a fixed pocket for the probe or a tool setter:

- Tormach PathPilot machines: the probe is **T99** by convention.
- A Hurco VMX30U (WinMax): the export on #2566 has `PROBE` as **T1**.
- A FANUC Robodrill (31i-A5): the owner's **T1** is the probe.

On the last two, CamCraft's first cutting tool becomes T1, so a posted program calls the probe for a face or drill operation. Found while making the Robodrill test kit (#2603): its first version faced with T01, and the owner answered "I will not face with my probe!". The kit was renumbered to T12-T15 by hand.

## Expected

- A machine file can name reserved tool numbers, for example `"tooling": { "reserved": [ { "number": 1, "use": "probe" } ] }` (the exact key to be decided).
- `add_tool` and the tool library skip those numbers for cutting tools; a probe tool takes the probe's number.
- `set_tool_number` to a reserved number for a tool of the wrong kind is refused by name (or warned), and verify/post warn when a program calls a reserved pocket for cutting.
- The Tormach machine files reserve T99 (probe); a generic VMC reserves nothing.

## Done means

A test with a machine file that reserves T1 for the probe: the first added end mill gets T2, the probe gets T1, and a program that cuts with T1 is refused by name.

## Goal

Check CamCraft's built-in **Fanuc** post on a real Fanuc control: a **FANUC Robodrill, 3-axis, control 31i-A5**, owned by @vilts, who also checks the Hurco post (#2573). The control has a graphic toolpath check, so each program can be checked before anything cuts.

What the owner uses on this machine: **G05.1 Q1 R1** (AI contour control), **rigid tapping**, and a turret ATC with no tool preload (T and M6 on one block).

## Open questions for the post

1. **Rigid tapping:** the post writes `G84 ... F` with no `M29`. On a 31i, G84 is rigid without M29 only when parameter 5200 bit 0 is set. Does this machine need `M29 S..` before G84? If so: a post option (or the default) that writes `M29 S..`.
2. **Peck cycle:** the post writes `G73` (chip break) for a peck drill, at `R0.` (the part top) after a rapid to Z0. Is G73 the right default, or G83 (full retract)? Should R be 1-2 mm above the top?

Asked by mkinney (2026-11-18): "If we get confused by those terms, then so will users/others. Make sure it is clear in the docs."

Two different things are both called "mill-turn":

Done means: the glossary is in those three places, and a search of the docs for "mill-turn" finds no use that leaves the meaning open.

title: sccache: crates with a build script, and solidcore below them, miss the cache in each new worktree

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P5
labels.description: Agent surface and tooling keep up with what shipped

body:
Found during the idle-box Linux measurement of #914 (https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/issues/914#issuecomment-6991514439). Part of the #900 build cycle work.

## What happens

A fresh worktree with a warm sccache cache reaches its first app test no faster than a build without sccache. On a 12-core Linux box: 274 s with a warm cache, 264 s without sccache. The #900 goal is 3x faster.

`cargo build --timings` of a warm run (282 s wall):
- `solidcore 1.0.1` compiles for 216 s, on the critical path.
- All `camcraft-*` units together take 41 s. The first one starts at 250 s.

`solidcore` is a cache miss in each new worktree:
- The sccache hash key of `solidcore` changes with the worktree (`94ef89da...` in one worktree, `78bb5f5e...` in another). The tree and the flags are the same.
- In the same worktree, `cargo clean -p solidcore` and a rebuild gives a hit in 3 s.

The crates that miss in a new worktree are the crates with a build script, and all crates that depend on them:
- Build scripts: `serde`, `serde_core`, `thiserror`, `num_traits`, `crc32fast`, one `proc_macro2` variant.
- Dependents: `serde_json`, `flate2`, `miniz_oxide`, `rayon`, `spade`, `solidcore`, `solidcore-record`, `solidcore-ops`, `solidcore-step`, `solidcore-convert`, `solidcore-tess`.

The `.rmeta` of these crates is not the same in two worktrees (for example, `libserde-aab1de1362e9bc28.rmeta` has a different md5). This agrees with an `OUT_DIR` below each worktree's own `target/`.

`SCCACHE_BASEDIRS` (sccache 0.18.0) with the two worktree roots does not change this. `serde`, `thiserror` and `solidcore` stay misses.

## Expected

A fresh worktree with a warm cache does not compile `solidcore` again. Each worktree compiles only our own crates (the #900 intent).

## Possible directions (not tested)

- Make the build-script crates give the same inputs in each worktree, so that sccache can hit them.
- Share the compiled dependencies between worktrees in a different way. Note: AGENTS.md forbids a shared `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`.
- Make `solidcore` cheaper in dev builds (for example, its `opt-level`), and measure the effect on the suites that use it.

## Environment

Linux (Manjaro), 12 cores, 32 GB RAM, rustc 1.98.0, sccache 0.18.0, `upstream/main` `c605e5687`. At `7cab31eea`, the dev profile, the `solidcore` pin and the sccache code in `xtask/src/exec.rs` are the same.

## Labels

I cannot set labels (no triage access). Suggested: `P7`, `effort:medium`, `area:build`. Filed by an agent session for a contributor, thus `source:agent` also applies.

Done means: a fresh worktree with a warm sccache cache gets a cache hit for `solidcore`, and the time to the first app test is measured and posted against the #914 numbers.

body:
Asked for by Mike (collaborator) on 2026-11-18: SolidCraft shows "update available" in its title bar; a click downloads the latest version and installs it. CamCraft has nothing like it - a user only finds a new release on GitHub.

Wanted:
1. **Check:** at start (and at most once a day), read the latest release tag from GitHub (`api.github.com/repos/NeoTech/Camcraft/releases/latest`). No account, no telemetry; a setting turns it off; offline or rate-limited = silent, never an error dialog. Never in the browser (wasm) build.
2. **Show:** a small "Update available: vX.Y.Z" item at the right of the title bar, next to the version (#352). Its tooltip names the version and links the release notes.
3. **Install on click** - the hard part, because the app is running:
   - Download the asset for this platform (Windows zip/installer, macOS, Linux tar/AppImage, FreeBSD) to a temp folder and check its SHA-256 against the release (the release needs a checksum file - today it has none) before anything runs.
   - Unsaved work: ask to save first (the usual unsaved-changes prompt); never drop work.
   - Replace and restart: a running exe cannot be overwritten on Windows. Usual pattern: quit, let a small helper (or the installer itself) swap the files and start the new version; or rename the running exe aside and put the new one in place, then restart. Package-manager installs (AUR, Homebrew, a .deb) are not self-updated: show "update available" with the command to run instead.
   - Failure at any step leaves the old version working and says what failed.
4. Never auto-install without a click; never download in the background without the setting allowing it.

Done means: on Windows and one of macOS/Linux, a build that is one release behind shows "Update available", a click updates it and restarts on the new version with the project reopened; a corrupt download (bad checksum) is refused with a message and the old version still starts; with the setting off or offline, nothing is shown and nothing fails.

Clean-room note: this is ordinary desktop-app behaviour (no Autodesk material involved). SolidCraft (our sister project) is a reference for the user experience only.

title: Tool body: a holder band that only touches the shank top widens the judged shank

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
Found during #2176 (PR #2179).

## What happens

`HolderProfile::enclose` (`crates/tools/src/holder_profile.rs`) sets the judged `shank_d` from `reach_over(flute_len, shank_top)`. `reach_over` uses inclusive bounds (`b.above <= hi && b.above + b.len >= lo`). Thus a holder band that starts exactly at the shank top widens the full judged shank to the band radius.

Example: the catalog tool `EM-0400-2FL` (Ø12 shank) with a drawn cone holder from r 10 to r 30 at the shank top. The judged `shank_d` is 60 mm. The shank laws then sweep a Ø60 shank from the flute top to the holder foot.

## Why it matters

The result is conservative, so it is not a gouge. But it can refuse a legal program: a shank law can report a collision that the real Ø12 shank does not make.

## Open questions

- Must the bound be exclusive at the shank top, or must only the band part below the shank top count?
- Which tests pin the current widening on purpose (#368, #828)?

Done means: a test pins that a band that only touches the shank top does not widen the judged shank, and no collision law reads a smaller body than the real one.

This is under the safety floor (a collision check), so it is `effort:high`.

- Reuse `crates/geometry/src/geo2d.rs` (`Region`, `Loop`, `Point2`, `Region::offset_sharp`) and `crates/geometry/src/geo2d/sweep.rs` (`Region::sweep`).

  - Inflate `Outside` outer loops by `cut_width + part_gap / 2`.
  - Inflate `OnLine` outer loops by `cut_width / 2 + part_gap / 2`.

  - Support router single-slot clearance mode (`part_gap >= cut_width`) when adjacent outside profiles share a single cutter-width channel.
- Shrink the usable sheet inward by `edge_margin` (plus outer `cut_width` clearance) via `Region::offset_sharp`.
- Compute No-Fit Polygons (NFP) and Inner-Fit Polygons (IFP) on the `geo2d::SCALE` (1-micron) grid.

  - Sort parts by decreasing area first. Break ties by part id and instance index.
  - Try candidate rotations (and mirroring only when `allow_mirror` is true).
  - Place small parts inside usable closed holes (`IFP(hole_usable, part_inflated)`) when `allow_parts_in_holes` is true.
  - Open new sheets when parts do not fit on active sheets.

## What is missing

An operation has no way to name model faces or edges that the tool must not touch. The user cannot protect a finished surface, a datum face or a sharp edge from a later operation.

1. Add a "Do not touch" selection to the Boundaries group of the Geometry tab of an operation.

3. Add a clearance parameter (default 0, the stock to leave still applies). The tool stays this distance from each protected item.
4. Each generator that the operation type uses keeps the tool clear of the protected items. This includes the cutting moves, the lead moves, the link moves and the plunges. The check uses the full tool: flutes, shank and holder.
5. The verify gate checks each generated move against the protected items. This check is independent of the generator.
6. If a move touches a protected item, the operation is refused or marked "incomplete" with a diagnostic that names the item. The post is blocked. The program is never posted with such a move (AGENTS.md "Prime Directive: Never Crash, Never Gouge").
7. If a protected item is also in the machining selection of the same operation, refuse the selection when the command is created. Say which item is in the two lists.
8. The project file stores the selection. Say in the PR if older builds refuse the new file.

This work is under the safety floor. It adds a gouge law and can change posted G-code for an operation that has protected items. An operation without protected items must give the same toolpath as before: pin that.

Part of #1490.

The rest generator currently trusts an entered previous tool. It assumes that tool cut the pocket to the requested depth.

Add a previous-operations mode that derives remaining material from the stock those operations actually leave.

Design decision:
- Keep the entered-tool mode explicit. Add a separate previous-operations mode through an undoable command, the project file, and MCP.
- Read only earlier operations in the same setup, in their actual order. Reuse the established carried-stock infrastructure.
- Require current operation paths and compatible setup coordinates. Refuse missing, stale, or unsupported stock by name, or mark the result incomplete.
- Read remaining stock at every requested cut depth. A shallow roughing pass does not prove that the lower floor is clear.
- Include tool shape, wall and floor allowances, and the supported simulation resolution. Unknown cells remain occupied.
- Pass a conservative remaining-material region to the motion generator. Do not infer cleared volume from the previous tool diameter alone.
- Invalidate the result when an earlier operation changes, moves, is suppressed, or changes its tool or depth.
- Keep the current stock backend. Do not combine this feature with the field-engine migration in #586 or #637.

Tests:
- Compare the rest region with independently simulated earlier operations.
- Test mixed previous tool sizes, bull-nose tools, partial depths, wall allowances, islands, and disconnected cuts.
- Test missing paths, stale paths, operation reordering, changed tools, and unsupported stock frames.
- Prove the plan never removes material from its rest estimate unless the earlier cuts prove that material absent.
- Prove command undo, project save and reopen, MCP editing, and dependency invalidation.
- Remove each depth and stock-validity guard separately. Each mutation must fail its pinning test.

Done means: previous-operations mode uses conservative stock at each depth, passes these tests, and never guesses when stock cannot be established.

Related: #586 and #637 migrate the stock representation. This issue consumes the current representation for 2D rest machining.

labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
The depth ladder of the depth-stepping operations keeps the remainder in the last step. Some users expect equal steps.

What happens:

- The shared level law `camcraft_motion::machining2d::cut_levels` steps down by the full stepdown from Top Z.
- The last level ends at Bottom Z exactly. The last step is the remainder.
- Example: Top Z 20, Bottom Z 2, stepdown 5 gives the levels `[15, 10, 5, 2]`. The last step is 3 mm. The other steps are 5 mm.

The other choice:

- Equal steps: the same number of levels, `ceil(span / stepdown)`, and each step is `span / count`.
- The same example gives four steps of 4.5 mm: `[15.5, 11, 6.5, 2]`.
- Each step stays at or below the stepdown. The load on the tool is more equal, and the last pass is not a light rub.

Where it came from: found while fixing #2004 (the ladder now starts one stepdown under Top Z). The fix kept the remainder and recorded this choice in `docs/decisions/2004-top-z-level.md`, decision 7.

Notes:

- This changes posted G-code of each depth-stepping operation (safety floor: `effort:high`).
- By the project rule "CAM choices are parameters", equal steps is an operation parameter with a default, not a silent change of the law.
- The callers are listed in the audit table of the PR for #2004.

Done means:

- A decision says which ladder is the default, and if the other is a parameter.
- If a parameter is added: it is on each depth-stepping operation, it is undoable through `EditOperationParams`, it has an MCP field, and a test pins the levels of the two modes.

title: Tool editor overhaul: labels left, cutting data by material, one preview, holders from the library

labels.name: source:agent

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
The maintainer asked for this in chat on 2026-11-15, on v0.21.0. His words:

> The tool editor page needs a re work, Input fields sitting left of the input, cutting data by material should be default behavior and the default "value" is what we have in the catalog now. We can have a material called "Unknown" that is the default value.  Why there is two previews of the tool is also strange. One drawn profile of the tool and the holder picked should be enough. The holder library, should remove the parametric holder values and "fill them in" with the values from the library.. There is no need for having a Weldon for each "sized tool".. a weldon is a weldon, and whatever tool will fit it.
> In general the Tool editor needs a complete overhaul.

This is an umbrella issue. Research it, then file one sub-issue for each part, and close this issue.

## Parts

1. **Layout.** Put each label on the left of its input field, in a property grid (see the Fusion-style dialog rule: collapsible groups, tooltips).
2. **Cutting data by material is the default.** Each tool has cutting data (speed, feed, stepdown, stepover) for each material. The current single set of values becomes the data of a material named `Unknown`. `Unknown` is the default material. Existing tool libraries and project files load with their values moved to `Unknown`, with no loss.
3. **One preview.** The editor shows one drawing: the tool profile and the holder that the user selected. Remove the second preview. (See #2005: the body and the spun profile draw over each other.)
4. **Holders come from the holder library.** The user selects a holder from the library. The holder values (diameter, length, gauge length) come from the library entry and are not typed into each tool. Remove the parametric holder fields from the tool.
5. **A holder is not sized to a tool.** One holder entry (for example a Weldon holder) serves each tool whose shank fits it. Do not keep one holder entry for each tool size. The fit check (shank diameter against the holder bore) must give a clear refusal when a tool does not fit.

## Questions for the research

- The tool library and project file format change (parts 2, 4, 5). Give the migration and the version bump. This can be a breaking change.
- How the collision check and the simulation get the holder shape after part 4. They must use the same shape that the preview shows.
- Where cutting data by material connects to the operation: the operation uses the material of the setup stock, or `Unknown` when the stock has no material.
- How this joins #2002 (tool settings in Properties, catalog in its own panel). Decide one layout for the two issues.

## Related

#2002, #2003, #2005, #93, #743, #808, #898

## Done means

Each part has a sub-issue with a priority, an effort label and a "Done means" line. This issue lists them and is closed.

title: Circular (ramp entry): stay at depth between levels instead of retracting to the clearance height and rapiding back to the cut floor

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
What happens: a Circular operation with entry Ramp (helical, after PR #1663) retracts to the clearance height after every depth level, then rapids straight back down to the floor it just cut, then starts the next helix. Seen in a PathPilot Hub run on the 770MX simulator, 2026-11-14 (file `hub-tests/1663-circular-ramp/pr.nc`, PR head 8d63209a; T4 4 mm end mill; 6 mm hole, two rings r 0.0394 and r 0.0197; steps 0.0394 in):

```
G3 X-1.3386 Y0.1142 Z-0.0987 I0.0394 J0 F19.69   (last ring of the level)
G0 X-1.3386 Y0.1142 Z0.1969                       (rapid up to clearance)
G0 X-1.3386 Y0.1142 Z-0.0987                      (rapid down to the floor just cut)
G3 X-1.4066 Y0.1412 Z-0.1037 I-0.0394 J0 F19.69   (next helix starts)
```

It is safe: the moves are straight up and down at one X/Y inside the cut hole. But:
- Each level adds an air trip to the clearance height and back. That costs time on a deep hole with many levels.
- The rapid down ends exactly on the previous floor, with no gap. A rapid usually stops a small clearance above the floor, and the last part is fed.

Wanted: between depth levels of one Circular operation, either
- (a) stay at depth: the next helix continues from the end of the last ring with no retract (the material below is uncut, and the helix ramps into it), or
- (b) if a retract is kept, rapid down only to a small clearance above the previous floor (for example the operation's ramp clearance), then feed the rest.

(a) is preferred. A retract should stay only where the tool must leave the hole (the last level, or a level change that needs a lift). The ramp entry and the refusals stay unchanged. The posted G-code changes, so update the circular goldens with the reason.

Found while running the Hub check for PR #1663 (issue #1609).

Done means: a pin shows no rapid to the clearance height between levels of one Circular operation (or, with option b, no rapid that ends below the previous floor plus the clearance). The circular goldens are updated, and the stock simulation still shows no gouge.

Found while working #984.

**What happens:** the same commit plans the same part differently on two platforms. `app pocket3d_hsm::the_users_bore_roughs_adaptive_level_by_level_and_verifies_clean` (release) on ecb54b7f:

| platform | rings levels | moves / planar / arcs |
|---|---|---|
| Windows (the #850 measure, PR #865) | Z 20.000 | 5530 / 5497 / 600 |
| macOS, Apple silicon (Homebrew rustc 1.99.1) | Z 20.000 (crossing at -2.33, -2.78) | 5786 / 5753 / 651 |

macOS is deterministic run to run, so it is not hash-map order. Rust does not contract `a*b+c` into FMA unless asked, so the most likely cause is the platform libm: `f64::sin`, `cos`, `atan2`, `hypot`, `exp`, `powf` call the system math library (MSVC CRT, glibc, Apple libm), which are not correctly rounded and differ in the last place. The STEP tessellation and the adaptive planner both use them, and the planner's crossing and acceptance tests are knife edges a 16 nm change flips (#882, #982). Not yet confirmed which call sites diverge, and not run on Linux.

**Why it matters:** a toolpath (and so the posted G-code) for the same part, tool and parameters depends on the OS the user runs. Every output is still verified and a crossing plan is refused by name, so this is not a gouge; but golden counts and exact plan pins cannot hold across platforms, and a user can see a different path from the same project file on two machines.

**Possible directions (open):** route the geometry and planner transcendental calls through a pure-Rust deterministic libm (the `libm` crate is already in Cargo.lock) so every platform rounds the same; or make the planner's decisions robust to sub-micron perturbation (#882, #982). Either changes toolpaths and needs every adaptive fixture re-measured.

Done means: the cause is confirmed on a second platform (Windows or Linux run of the bore test, plus which calls diverge), and either the output is made platform-identical with goldens re-measured, or the decision not to is recorded.

Refs #984, #882, #982.

Second step of the maintainer's decision of 2026-11-11 to replace truck with solidcore (first step: #916, the bench).

What: `crates/app`'s STEP import (`crates/app/src/geometry/import/step*.rs`) goes through the kernel seam's solidcore STEP importer; every import test, golden and fixture keeps its verdict or the change is listed and decided; then `truck-*` and `ruststep` leave `Cargo.toml` and `Cargo.lock` (which also ends the ruststep git pin - #909 closes with this), and truck's kernel role is retired as #27 says.

Blocked on: #916 (the agreement bench must agree, and its tessellation answer decides how the mesh is made here).

Safety floor: imported geometry is what every toolpath and gouge check is judged against. The unit handling (#306, #689), the chord caps (#689, #864), the reduced-fidelity flag (#864 / PR #911) and the corrupt-input laws must all hold on the new importer, each with its existing pin.

Still open when this lands: the solidcore crates themselves are a git pin until upstream publishes them - a follow-up issue like #909 is filed then.

Part of #27.

Done means: no `truck-*` or `ruststep` package in `Cargo.lock`; the import suites, the STEP unit and chord suites and the release tier are green; IGES stays refused by name unless #27 says otherwise.

title: Process changes - fork maintainers please subscribe

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: P?
labels.description: Paused: never picked until the maintainer sets a real priority

body:
**Subscribe to this issue** (the "Subscribe" button on the right) if you work from a fork of CamCraft, especially with an AI agent.

Forks sync product code only at release tags (AGENTS.md "A fork syncs from upstream at each cut tag"). But the *process* - `AGENTS.md`, the agent definitions in `.claude/agents/`, the skills in `.claude/skills/` and `scripts/gate.*` - changes between releases, and a fork's agents should follow the current rules (review labels, priority labels, release steps, and so on).

**How it works:**
- `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` holds one number. Every PR that changes a process file bumps it.
- Every such PR also adds a comment **here**: the new version, what changed, and what to pull. Subscribers get one notification per change.
- A fork's agent compares its `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` with upstream's at the start of each session and, if upstream is newer, pulls just the process files (AGENTS.md "Process files sync on every session"). Product code still waits for the next release tag.

**To pull by hand:**
```
git fetch upstream
git checkout upstream/main -- AGENTS.md .claude/agents .claude/skills .claude/PROCESS_VERSION scripts/gate.ps1 scripts/gate.sh
git commit -m "chore(process): sync process files to upstream PROCESS_VERSION <n>"
```

This issue stays open and pinned. It's labelled `P?` so no agent ever picks it up as work.
